While children around the world return to school, Gaza’s children are entering their third consecutive year without an education. More than 90% of schools in Gaza have been damaged or reduced to ruins amid Israel’s unrelenting genocide. 22,000+ Palestinian children slaughtered. 44,000+ injured. Thousands remain missing. Likely martyred and still beneath the rubble. While children elsewhere put on new uniforms, carry new school bags and look forward to seeing their friends, children in Gaza are fighting simply to survive. Children are deliberately sniped as target practice and killed including for flying kites. Childhood stolen. Thousands orphaned. Children have been forced into the role of parents, caring for younger siblings after their parents martyred. The suffering doesn't stop at Gaza. In the West Bank, 84 Palestinian schools currently face demolition or orders to stop educating, leaving almost 13,000 students uncertain whether their schools will exist tomorrow. All of this unfolding against the backdrop of Israel’s continuing occupation and expansion of illegal settlements. For Palestinian children, school should mean learning, not survival. Childhood should mean safety, not fear. A Free Palestine A free Palestine represents the hope that Palestinians can live with freedom, dignity, security, and equal human rights. For generations, Palestinians have experienced displacement, occupation, conflict, restrictions on movement, and the loss of homes and communities. Behind the political debate are ordinary people who want to live their lives, raise their families, study, work, and build a peaceful future. Supporting a free Palestine means recognizing the humanity and rights of Palestinian people. It means believing that Palestinians deserve the freedom to determine their own future and to live without discrimination, forced displacement, or violence. It also means recognizing that Israeli civilians deserve safety and security, and that Palestinian and Israeli lives should not be treated as less valuable than one another. Peace cannot be built through endless violence or by denying the rights of an entire population. A lasting peace requires dignity, freedom, security, justice, and respect for human rights. It requires protecting civilians, rejecting attacks against civilians, and creating conditions in which both Palestinians and Israelis can live without fear. The Palestinian people deserve the opportunity to build their own future. Children deserve schools instead of destruction, families deserve homes instead of displacement, and young people deserve opportunities instead of growing up surrounded by conflict. Freedom for Palestine should not mean hatred toward another people. It should mean freedom from oppression and a future based on equality, dignity, and peace. The hope is for a future in which Palestinians can live freely in their homeland and Israelis can live safely as well. A better future is possible when human rights are respected for everyone. Freedom, justice, dignity, and peace should not belong to only one people. They should belong to all. Free Palestine. 🇵🇸 Peace for Palestinians. Peace for Israelis.
